original_question: Is every c.e. degree, or at least some c.e. degree, the degree of topological categoricity of a computable Polish space?
target_in_paper: Section 8 (Keng Meng Selwyn Ng), Problem 29, read together with the definition paragraph immediately before Problem 27. Problem 29 asks whether every/any c.e. degree is the degree of topological categoricity, and the preceding paragraph defines d-categoricity and the degree of topological categoricity for computable Polish spaces. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual question: it correctly identifies c.e. degrees as the target degree class, it correctly places the problem in the setting of computable Polish spaces, and it preserves the paper’s two-level scope ('every' c.e. degree, or at least 'some' c.e. degree). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
missing_details: The paper is talking about Turing degrees, so 'c.e. degree' here means a computably enumerable Turing degree. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

The existential quantifier over spaces should be made explicit: for a given c.e. degree a, the question is whether there exists some computable Polish space X whose degree of topological categoricity is exactly a. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
The phrase 'degree of topological categoricity' needs to be unpacked: it is the least Turing degree d such that X is d-categorical. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

And X is d-categorical precisely when, for every pair of computable metric spaces M and N that are homeomorphic to X, there is a d-computable homeomorphism from M onto N. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

The paper’s wording 'every/any' compresses two nested questions, both of which should be preserved: first, whether every c.e. degree is realizable; second, if not, whether at least one c.e. degree is realizable. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

No additional algebraic ambient data or asymptotic qualifiers occur here; the missing content is entirely in the computable-topological definitions and quantifiers. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
refined_question: Does every computably enumerable Turing degree a—and, if not, does at least one computably enumerable Turing degree—occur as the degree of topological categoricity of some computable Polish space X; that is, as the least Turing degree d such that whenever M and N are computable metric spaces homeomorphic to X, there is a d-computable homeomorphism from M onto N?
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem 29 in Section 8. The immediately preceding paragraph supplies the hidden assumptions your draft leaves implicit: the relevant degrees are Turing degrees, d-categoricity is defined via d-computable homeomorphisms between arbitrary computable metric presentations of the same computable Polish space, and the degree of topological categoricity is the least such degree. The paper does not give a nearby theorem, proposition, or remark proving an equivalent reformulation of Problem 29, so the faithful refinement is simply to spell out those definitions and quantifiers without broadening the scope. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
